title: El Puro de San Andrés, MEXI STORIES
comment: puro-tuxtla (MEXI): galera de torcido de puros de una hacienda tabacalera en San Andrés Tuxtla, Veracruz, a media mañana. Caras comunes, no famosas; los cuatro se distinguen a simple vista.

chars.ELVIRA_SANTAMARIA: Mexican woman, feared owner of a tobacco hacienda, 60 years old, fair skin, short sleek silver bob haircut, sharp dark eyes, deep red lipstick, a tailored black linen dress with long sleeves, a thick gold bracelet, gold-rimmed reading glasses hanging on a chain, her hands empty.
chars.AZUCENA_MORA: Mexican woman, new cigar roller, 30 years old, brown skin, black hair in a tight bun with a few loose strands, focused dark eyes, a simple sleeveless cream cotton blouse, a long brown skirt, a plain leather bracelet, her hands empty.
chars.ANACLETO_BARRERA: Mexican man, the hacienda's long-time foreman, 52 years old, tanned skin, a big black mustache with grey hairs, a round face, small eyes, a white guayabera stained with tobacco, a brown leather belt with a ring of old keys, a straw hat, his hands empty.
chars.IVAN_SANTAMARIA: Mexican man, the owner's son, 33 years old, light-brown skin, short dark hair, a neat short beard, kind honest eyes, a light-grey linen shirt with rolled sleeves, beige trousers, his hands empty.

locs.LOC_GALERATUXTLA: Cigar rolling room of an old tobacco hacienda in San Andres Tuxtla, Veracruz, in the mid-morning: long wooden rolling tables with bundles of brown tobacco leaves, wooden cigar molds, dried tobacco leaves hanging from the high wooden ceiling, white walls, tall open windows onto green tobacco fields, warm humid light, no readable text, no signs, no logos, no people.
